svg.title: BCBC 2024 · 9.20.11.1 Anchorage to Floor or Roof Assemblies where Masonry Walls Require Lateral Support
svg.text: BCBC 2024 · DIVISION B · PART 9 HOUSING AND SMALL BUILDINGS · SECTION 9.20 MASONRY AND INSULATING CONCRETE FORM WALLS NOT IN CONTACT WITH THE GROUND
Anchorage to Floor or Roof Assemblies where Masonry Walls Require Lateral Support

g.text: Anchor to each floor or roof assembly at
intervals of not more than 2 m (6′-6¾″), (1)
Joists at right angles to the wall, (1)
Joists parallel to the wall: anchors extend
Corrosion-resistant strap, not less than the
Securely fastened to the joist to develop
the full strength of the anchor, (3)
Shaped to key mechanically with the masonry, (3)
Floor joists not more than 1 m (3′-3⅜″) above

svg.text: WHAT THE CODE REQUIRES
Where masonry walls are required to receive
lateral support (Subsection 9.20.10.), they
are anchored to each floor or roof assembly at
maximum intervals of 2 m (6′-6¾″)
Anchorage to floor joists not more than 1 m
(3′-3⅜″) above grade may be omitted.
The anchors are corrosion-resistant and not
less than the equivalent of 40 mm by 4.76 mm
thick steel straps.
The anchors are shaped to provide a mechanical
key with the masonry and are securely fastened
to the horizontal support to develop the full
strength of the anchor.
When joists are parallel to the wall, the
anchors extend across not less than 3 joists.
Drawn: A, B anchors schematic, dashed where in the wall, subfloor not shown. C on the cut face. D height measured to the joist underside.
Source: BCBC 2024, Division B, Article 9.20.11.1. (page 9-148)
